To install Loguru, use the command `pip install loguru` as stated in the repository's main documentation. For development purposes, clone the repository with `git clone git@github.com:your_name_here/loguru.git`, activate a virtual environment with `python -m venv env` and `source env/bin/activate`, and then install Loguru in development mode with `pip install -e ".[dev]"`. Additionally, pre-commit hooks can be installed with `pre-commit install --install-hooks`.
To install the loguru Python library, use the command `pip install loguru`. The library aims to simplify Python logging by providing useful functionalities that address the limitations of standard loggers. The sources indicate that loguru is compatible with both CPython and PyPy implementations of Python. While the documentation suggests a minimal setup with `from loguru import logger`, the sources also mention that the repository lacks beginner-friendly documentation, recommending the "Take the tour" section in the README for a quick preview.
The sources indicate that Loguru is a library which aims to bring enjoyable logging in Python. The "lager" source mentions that Lager is a utility pack for Loguru and suggests checking out Loguru from its GitHub page: https://github.com/Delgan/loguru. The "beans-logging" source describes itself as a Loguru based custom logging package for Python projects. The "loguru" source on PyPI confirms Loguru's purpose as a library for Python logging. The sources do not provide specific installation requirements for Loguru.

model_claims.text: With rotation=["13:00","12:00"], a file created at 06:00 and two log messages after idle until 13:00:01 results in exactly two log files (the original and one rotated) rather than three files (including a spurious extra rotation).
model_claims.source_quote:
before — 3 files (BUG):
  file.2020-01-01_06-00-00_000000.log     'a\n'
  file.2020-01-01_13-00-01_000000.log     'b\n'    <-- spurious extra rotation
  file.log                                'c\n'
after — 2 files (correct):
  file.2020-01-01_06-00-00_000000.log     'a\n'
  file.log                                'b\nc\n'

model_claims.text: The function still returns True if any rotation condition would trigger, preserving the documented 'any of which can trigger the rotation' contract for the return value.
model_claims.source_quote: This keeps the documented 'any of which can trigger the rotation' contract for the return value while restoring the side effect the conditions rely on.

model_rejected_claims.text: Evaluating every rotation condition (instead of using any() short-circuit) prevents a skipped condition from firing spuriously on the next logged message.
model_rejected_claims.source_quote: Note that the conditions must all be evaluated, even after one of them returned True, because "RotationTime" instances keep their limit up-to-date as a side-effect of being called. Skipping them would leave a stale limit in the past, causing a spurious extra rotation on the next logged message.
